name: Fully Active Records Determine One Gluing-Behavior Class
statement: For a nonempty peelable ample common section $D$ and the rooted attachment factor $R$, the product piece $\Omega_D=D\times R$ has record set $\{(\pi,D):\pi\in\operatorname{Ord}(D)\}$. Every peelable piece all of whose records have active set $D$ is interchangeable with $\Omega_D$: its union with a test piece $C$ peels exactly when $C$ peels down to $D$. Moreover, every peelable piece failing to peel down to $D$ can be extended by at most $|D|-1$ further such failing pieces to a peelable piece in this fully active class.
proof: The exact context-record formula with attachment site $K=D$ gives the records of $\Omega_D$. Compatibility with a fully active record requires the test piece to have an empty-active record, which is equivalent to peeling down to $D$ and then holds for every order. Starting from any peelable nonidentity piece, repeatedly glue a test piece that distinguishes its class from the fully active class. Each added piece also fails to peel to $D$, while the union remains peelable. The $|D|+1$-factor nilpotence bound forces this process to stop after at most $|D|-1$ additions.
